solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Film starring e.g. Bruce Lee, arrogant about jumps?

indicators.note: one word placed about another wraps around it on both sides

parts.note: cocky means brashly self-confident
hops are small jumps

explanation.surface: A kung-fu star swaggering around, leaping about on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumps' sits so naturally beside a kung-fu film that it reads as action, not as a word to be enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopsocky is slang for a cheap martial-arts movie, the genre that made Bruce Lee famous.

clue.text: Players given guidance with solid defences

parts.note: the cast are the actors in a play
led means guided

explanation.surface: A team coached well ends up with a strong defence.
explanation.walkthrough: Players looks like a sports team, but they are actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Castled means fortified with castles, and in chess a castled king sits behind a solid wall of pawns.

clue.text: Sort of cornbread, one wrapped up in ham?

indicators.note: something wrapped in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: to hoke is to overact, to ham

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A cornbread loaf rolled up inside some ham.
explanation.walkthrough: Ham is the verb to overact, not the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoecake is a thin cake of cornmeal, said to have been baked on a hoe blade.

clue.text: Small coin like this is seen in circulation round Spain

definitions.text: Small coin like this is seen in circulation round Spain

indicators.note: the earlier letters are placed round the next, enclosing it

parts.note: p is a penny
so means in this way
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A modest coin of this kind changes hands all over Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer, a coin in circulation in Spain before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: The peso was Spain's old silver coin and is the currency unit of many Latin American countries.

clue.text: Musician, one accompanying harp in medley

definitions.note: the answer is usually an adjective, 'like Orpheus'

indicators.note: a medley is a jumble of tunes, so these letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician playing alongside a harp in a medley of tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpheus was the legendary Greek musician, so Orphean means like him, melodious and enchanting.

clue.text: The basics, including egg, covered with slice of Cheddar cheese

indicators.note: a slice is only a thin piece, so one letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter

indicators.note: something including another holds it inside

parts.note: the ABC of a subject is its basics
O looks like an egg

explanation.surface: Basic cooking: egg covered with a slice of Cheddar.
explanation.walkthrough: Covered with means C sits on top of the rest, as this is a down clue. Cheddar is a decoy; the answer is a different cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Caboc is a rich Scottish cream cheese rolled in oatmeal.

clue.text: Roast fish served in a hulk at seas

indicators.note: the fish is served inside the other letters
at sea means confused, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Roast fish dished up aboard an old ship at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Roast is the verb to scold harshly, not cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: To keelhaul is to rebuke severely, from the old naval punishment of dragging a sailor under the keel.

clue.text: Bit of armour I glue on, mixing up lesson from the past

indicators.note: mixing up throws these letters into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
lere is an archaic word for lesson or teaching

explanation.surface: Someone sticking armour together in a muddle, learning an old lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A genouillère is the knee-piece of a suit of armour, from French genou, knee.

clue.text: Accepted ring, imitation?

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for accepted
a ping is a ringing sound

explanation.surface: Someone accepts a ring, but is it a fake?
explanation.definitionFit: Aping, as a noun, is copying someone's behaviour, a mimicking imitation.

clue.text: Article without core and then put out of order providing effective power

indicators.note: out of order means jumbled, the letters rearranged
without its core means the centre letter is cut out

parts.note: the definite article; used twice

explanation.surface: A broken-down item stops a machine delivering power.
explanation.walkthrough: The article is used twice: first with its middle H removed, then complete but rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth means the force to make something effective, as in a law with teeth.

clue.text: Aluminium silicate I put in grinder's turned up in tea oddly

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read upwards, backwards
the letter is put in, placed inside the word

parts.note: a mill is a grinder; mill's, apostrophe dropped
taken as written

indicators.note: arranged oddly means in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mineral ground up in a grinder appears oddly in your tea.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into MILLS before the last S; the result is reversed, then IN TEA rearranged follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Sillimanite is a mineral consisting of aluminium silicate, named after the chemist Benjamin Silliman.

clue.text: Peepers excited about a star group

indicators.note: the shuffled word goes around the single letter that follows
excited letters are stirred up and jump about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Eager eyes stare excitedly at a cluster of stars.
explanation.walkthrough: Peepers is slang for eyes, which suits stargazing, but here the word is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Praesepe, the Beehive Cluster in Cancer, is an open cluster of stars visible to the naked eye.

clue.text: Trembler rarely in grip of disease is malingering

indicators.note: the run of letters is held within the grip of the words that follow

parts.note: found running across the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone shaking with illness may simply be faking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' is part of the definition: Chambers marks the word as uncommon.
explanation.definitionFit: A seism is an earthquake, a shaking of the ground, so a rare word for a trembler.

clue.text: Gathering round exotic bird in little hat

indicators.note: one word is set round another, enclosing it

parts.note: a bee is a social gathering for work, as in a sewing bee
the ani is a tropical American cuckoo

explanation.surface: A crowd gathers round a rare bird wearing a tiny hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanie is a small close-fitting brimless cap.

clue.text: Plain cotton that's half absorbing dried blood?

indicators.note: something absorbing takes another thing inside itself
only half the letters of the word are kept, the front pair

parts.note: the first half of this four-letter word
a clot is a lump of congealed blood

explanation.surface: A plain fabric that soaks up dried bloodstains, as a bandage might.
explanation.definitionFit: T-cloth is a plain-woven cotton fabric, once stamped with a T and exported to Asia.

clue.text: Aganippe, say — might feet be suggested by this?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fountain or spring, Aganippe being the spring of the Muses on Helicon

definitions.text: might feet be suggested by this?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a set of printing type, which when jumbled is called pie or pied, and pied is French for foot

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint: a fount of type that gets mixed up is 'pied', the French word for a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Font is a poetic word for a fountain or spring, and also a complete set of type in one face and size.

clue.text: Sing along meaninglessly composition of Falla (not loud)

indicators.note: a composition puts its elements together in a fresh arrangement
the musical abbreviation for loud is told to be absent from the name

parts.note: the Spanish composer Manuel de Falla, taken as written
f, forte, is loud in music

explanation.surface: Humming along without words to a piece by Falla, played softly.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove F from FALLA to leave ALLA, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To la-la is to sing nonsense syllables, a tune without real words.

clue.text: French gateau, nutty stuff once carried on board

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for French

indicators.note: nutty means crazy, so the letters go wild

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A French cake with nuts, once loaded aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nutty' looks like a description of the cake, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Frautage is an obsolete form of freightage, goods carried as cargo on a ship.

clue.text: Surly lout, hard laid into hack

indicators.note: something laid into another is placed inside it

parts.note: to hack is to cough harshly
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A rude thug, beaten hard by a journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like a writer but is the verb to cough. H goes after the C of COUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists chough as a variant of chuff, a boor or churlish fellow.

clue.text: Coward maybe, in bother about lustreless lives

indicators.note: the exclamation is placed about the following words, surrounding them

parts.note: drat is a mild curse, like bother!
mat or matt means without sheen
is means exists, lives

explanation.surface: A timid person, troubled about a dull life.
explanation.walkthrough: Coward is Noël Coward, the English playwright, not a timid person.
explanation.definitionFit: Noël Coward wrote plays such as Private Lives, so he is an example of a playwright.

clue.text: Sword length swallowed by small type of shark

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside the swallower

parts.note: the morgay is the small-spotted dogfish, a small shark
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A sword's whole length gulped down by a small shark.
explanation.definitionFit: Morglay was the sword of Bevis of Hampton in romance, and so came to mean any sword.

clue.text: Very small sum added to reserve fund — most disagreeable

parts.note: a sou is an old French coin, a trifling amount
in banking the rest is a reserve fund

explanation.surface: A tiny amount added to the reserves is a nasty shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Sourest is the superlative of sour, meaning bad-tempered or unpleasant.

clue.text: Aid when playing organ runs in Satie's Capriccioso?

indicators.note: one letter goes in among the others
capriccioso means in a capricious, free style, so these letters are rearranged at whim

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A help for organ playing turns up in a capriccio by Satie.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirasse is an organ pedal coupler, a mechanism that lets the pedals play manual keys.

clue.text: Defunct uncle, one enshrined in grim bearing

indicators.note: something enshrined in another is set within it, as a relic in a shrine

parts.note: dour means stern, grim
eme is an obsolete word for an uncle
an is the article meaning one

explanation.surface: A dead uncle lies in state with a grim expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defunct' tells you the word for uncle is obsolete, not that he has died.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeanour is the way a person carries themselves, their manner or deportment.

clue.text: Like a drink? This is wildly gingery

parts.note: as means like
taken as written
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a fiery ginger cocktail is to your taste.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: asarum's common name is wild ginger, so the plant is 'wildly gingery'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asarum is the genus of plants called wild ginger, whose roots taste of ginger.

clue.text: Phoenician letter? One has help with translation

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: translation carries a word into another form, so its letters change order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone needs help translating a letter written by a Phoenician.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph is the first letter of the Phoenician and Hebrew alphabets.

clue.text: May June period, start of summer, terrible one?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter
Ivan the Terrible, tsar of Russia

explanation.surface: Early summer, between May and June, can be dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sivan is the ninth month of the Jewish civil year, falling in May and June.

clue.text: Frantically busy Old Trafford local maybe, hosting international

indicators.note: a host has a guest inside, so one item goes within another

parts.note: a Manc is a Mancunian; Old Trafford, Manchester United's ground, is in Greater Manchester
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A Manchester fan run off their feet hosting an international match.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic means wildly energetic and hectic, like someone with far too much to do.

clue.text: Bass trumpet in band creating fuzzy effect

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music
a lur is a long curved Bronze Age trumpet, revived in Scandinavian bands

explanation.surface: A bass trumpet playing in a band makes a muddy sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A blur is something seen indistinctly, a smudged or hazy appearance.

clue.text: Associate — more than one in Frankfurt is sinister

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to connect or join

definitions.text: more than one in Frankfurt is sinister
definitions.meaning: second meaning, cryptic: add the plural S and you have the German for left

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint: the plural of the word is German links, meaning left, and sinister is Latin for left.
explanation.definitionFit: To link is to associate or connect one thing with another.

clue.text: Less time to learn German? It could be normal with these classes

parts.note: surface padding for the picture of a shortened course

indicators.note: less here means minus, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: general means usual, normal
L is the learner's abbreviation
surface padding: the German class is pure scene-setting

explanation.surface: A German course is cut short; fewer lessons in the timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads loosely: with L for learner added, these classes could be normal. Less signals that the letter comes off the word for normal.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera, plural of genus, are classes in biological classification ranking above species.

clue.text: Part of central London given over for crown historically

indicators.note: turned over, the run of letters is read the other way
only part of the following words is taken

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A slice of central London handed over to the Crown in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Crown is the top of the head, not the monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Noll is an obsolete word for the head, the top or crown of it.

clue.text: Anaesthetic drug: doze I have when coming rounbd

indicators.note: coming round means turning about, so the letters face the other way

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
the contraction I've

explanation.surface: A patient dozes under anaesthetic and comes round afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rounbd' is the source's typo for round.
explanation.definitionFit: Evipan is a trade name for hexobarbital, a barbiturate once used as an intravenous anaesthetic.

clue.text: Company abandoned morris dance customs

indicators.note: what is abandoned is left out of the word

parts.note: a moresco is a Moorish dance, the morris dance
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A troupe has given up morris dancing, an old tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: MORESCO without CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Mores are the customs and conventions of a community, a Latin plural.

clue.text: Chum holding a flap I connected to a sort of parachute

definitions.text: connected to a sort of parachute

indicators.note: the friend is holding the next words inside itself

parts.note: a pal is a friend
taken as written
a tag is a hanging flap or loose end
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend clutching a flap attached to a parachute.
explanation.walkthrough: The sort of parachute is the patagium, the skin membrane a flying squirrel glides on.
explanation.definitionFit: Patagial means relating to the patagium, the stretched skin that lets gliding animals parachute.

clue.text: The sort of thing Greens approve of, turning powdery in experience I've lost

definitions.text: The sort of thing Greens approve of

indicators.note: the reversed word sits in the shortened one
the contraction is lost, removed from the word for experience

parts.note: to receive is to undergo, experience
taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: turning means the word is spun round to face backwards

parts.note: talcy means like talc, powdery

explanation.surface: Environmentalists approve of turning dust into something useful once you're past experience.
explanation.walkthrough: The contraction I've is taken off the end of the word for experience. Greens are environmentalists, from the Green Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Recyclate is material that has been or can be recycled, which environmentalists favour.
